correctness.rationale: PASS: For even x,z, F(x)-F(z)=(x-z)(x²+xz+z²-3) with odd unit factor, so exactly one even inverse for each even target. The exact decompositions F(x)+2=(x-1)²(x+2) and F(x)-2=(x+1)²(x-2) reduce odd inputs to valuation shells indexed by r>=2. For odd u,v in a common class mod4, v2(U(u)-U(v))=v2(u-v)+1; finite bijections imply both classes cover c_{±,r}+8Z2 and hence give two odd inverse points. Counting u modulo 2^{k-r} gives the complete piecewise exact counts 2^{floor(k/2)} or 2^{min(k-r-1,r+2)} at each shell; disjointness and measure are proved. Direct exhaustive target comparisons at every k=4..17 and normalization passed. The infinite proof does not rely on the finite tests.

value.rationale: PASS: The target-wise root count of X³−3X−y modulo 2^k is a natural arithmetic invariant of the first nontrivial odd-degree Dickson polynomial. The discriminant 27(4-y²) motivates singular critical targets ±2 before any computation. The result gives every finite congruence fiber, all actual 2-adic inverse points, sharp least periods and a nontrivial exact 1/48 Haar measure for the three-root locus. It explains singular valuation towers and the unusual difference between finite and infinite fibers, rather than a routine parity-image observation or an arbitrary numerical cutoff.
